facts.statement: Genusaurus is a genus of abelisaurid theropod dinosaurs whose name means "knee lizard".
facts.quote: Genusaurus ( ; meaning "knee lizard") is a genus of abelisaurid theropod from the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The pelvic elements of Genusaurus were strongly fused.
facts.quote: The elements of the pelvis are strongly fused.

facts.statement: Genusaurus had a cnemial crest on its tibia that extended strongly forward and curved upward.
facts.quote: The cnemial crest strongly extends to the front and is curved upwards.

facts.statement: In 2016, Genusaurus was estimated to be 3.6 meters long, making it one of the smallest known abelisaurids.
facts.quote: In 2016, its length was estimated at 3.6 m, making it among the smallest known abelisaurids.

facts.statement: Genusaurus lived during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 to 100 million years ago.
facts.quote: Genusaurus is believed to have lived during the Albian stage, around 112-100 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossils of Genusaurus have been found in France.
facts.quote: Its fossils were found in France.

facts.statement: Genusaurus sisteronis is the only named species within the genus Genusaurus.
facts.quote: The type species, Genusaurus sisteronis, is the only named species.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Genusaurus is a partial skeleton found between 1984 and 1986 in the Albian Bevons Beds.
facts.quote: It is based on a partial skeleton found in 1984-1986 in the Albian Bevons Beds, holotype MNHN Bev.1.

facts.statement: Genusaurus was named and described by Hugues Accarie and colleagues in 1995.
facts.quote: It was named and described by Hugues Accarie, Bernard Beaudoin, Jean Dejax, Gérard Friès, Jean-Guy Michard and Philippe Taquet in 1995.

facts.statement: The specific name sisteronis refers to the town of Sisteron near where the fossil was discovered.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to Sisteron, the town near which the specimen was found.

facts.statement: A 2008 analysis placed Genusaurus in the family Noasauridae alongside Laevisuchus, Masiakasaurus, Noasaurus, and Velocisaurus.
facts.quote: A 2008 cladistic analysis by Carrano and Sampson placed Genusaurus in the Noasauridae along with Laevisuchus, Masiakasaurus, Noasaurus, and Velocisaurus

facts.statement: In 2025, Eric Buffetaut suggested placing Genusaurus into Furileusauria, confirming its classification as an abelisaurid.
facts.quote: In 2025, Eric Buffetaut reexamined the holotype and suggested that it should be placed into Furileusauria, and confirming its abelisaurid classification.

facts.statement: Genusaurus is classified within the subfamily Majungasaurinae.
The time range for Genusaurus is estimated between 110.1 and 106.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus name Genusaurus refers to the cnemial crest located in front of the proximal end of the tibia.
rejected.quote: The genus name is derived from the Latin word genu (knee) and refers to the cnemial crest in front of the proximal end of the tibia.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'front of the proximal end of the tibia'
